title: Residual unguarded execution path: core/enhance.py calls execute_pipeline() without a JobManager job; direct CLI run bypasses submission
body: Found in PFSSOT-P0 reuse map. Doc section 43(c) requires no normal execution path silently bypasses JobManager. enhance + direct CLI run remain. Fix as part of P8A.

rcca.root_cause: core/enhance.py constructs a PipelineExecutor and calls execute_pipeline() without first going through job_manager/run_entry; it relies only on the executor's run-lock guard. Direct CLI scripts/run_pipeline.py likewise executes without a pre-existing JobManager job.
five_why: 1. Why does enhance run directly? It is a convenience wrapper written before the single-path rule.
2. Why is that a defect? It can execute work outside the scheduled/queued path (silent bypass).
3. Why is it not always caught? The executor's lock guard only blocks concurrent runs, not submission.
4. Why does it matter? The scheduler must own submission; unmetered paths break claim/lease semantics.
5. Why now? P8A gate requires no normal execution path bypasses JobManager.
rcca.corrective: core/enhance.py apply_and_run now submits via core.run_entry.enqueue instead of calling PipelineExecutor.execute_pipeline() directly; the queue/worker invokes the executor.
rcca.preventive: scripts/dev/single_path_check.py fails on any NEW direct execute_pipeline() outside the allowlist; also asserts core does not import the optional worker layer.
